title: SAF Airstrike on Balila Market and Water Source Kills 10 in Kurmuk Locality, Blue Nile State
detail: Sudanese Armed Forces conducted a drone/aerial strike on the Balila market area and a nearby water source in Kurmuk locality, Blue Nile State on May 4, 2026, killing at least 7–10 people and injuring 20 others, mostly women and children. The SPLM-N El Hilu (Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North, al-Hilu faction), which controls Kurmuk jointly with the RSF since the joint capture of the town on March 23, 2026, condemned the attack in a formal statement, reporting 10 killed and 20 injured. Assayha newspaper reported at least 7 killed. Fires broke out in market stalls and water infrastructure was also destroyed, according to Dabanga Radio TV Online. Livestock were also killed. Kurmuk locality in southeastern Blue Nile State, near the Ethiopia and South Sudan borders, has been an active frontline since RSF-SPLM-N forces seized Kurmuk on March 23, 2026 — when approximately 73,000 civilians fled and SAF's 16th Brigade withdrew. SAF has been conducting airstrikes against RSF-SPLM-N positions across Blue Nile State since the fall of Kurmuk, aiming to slow their push toward Ed Damazin and the Roseires Dam. SAF's 4th Infantry Division retook Muqja Station (April 21, 2026), partially restoring the Kurmuk–Damazin supply axis, but fighting continues across the Kurmuk locality. The strike on Balila market is in keeping with SAF's pattern of striking civilian and economic infrastructure in RSF-SPLM-N-controlled areas of Blue Nile State.

title: Gen. Burhan Visits Kaikal Family Compound in Gezira; Sovereign Council Issues Formal Condemnation of RSF Strike
detail: Sudan's head of state Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan traveled to the Al-Kahli Zaidan village in Al Jazirah (Gezira) State on the night of May 3-4, 2026 to offer official condolences following the RSF drone strike on May 2 that killed 9–17 family members of Sudan Shield Forces commander Abu Aqla Kaikal. The Sovereign Council — Sudan's nominal ruling body headed by al-Burhan — issued a formal statement condemning the RSF for the targeted attack on a civilian family compound. Al-Burhan's personal visit signals the political and strategic importance of the Sudan Shield Forces to SAF's war effort: Kaikal had defected from the RSF in October 2024 and played a key role in recapturing Al Jazirah State before advancing toward Khartoum. The Sovereign Council statement described the attack as a 'terrorist act' targeting innocent civilians, including women and children. The visit also reflects SAF's effort to maintain the loyalty of former RSF-defector commanders who have provided SAF with critical tactical intelligence and local forces. The National (UAE) published details of Burhan's condolence visit alongside the higher casualty figure of 17 killed (updated from AFP's initial 9 killed report). The RSF did not publicly claim responsibility for the May 2 strike.

media.caption: Gen. Burhan visits Kaikal family compound in Gezira; Sovereign Council condemns RSF targeted drone strike that killed 9–17 civilians, including children
